html:
SMTO-EXE-0146 — The button or field SMTO needs isn't visible on screen

GUID: 5471b3c9-7b8a-5a25-9d62-20d6078c9533
Slug: ui-element-not-visible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO found the button or field, but it's hidden, scrolled out of view or off the edge of the screen, so SMTO couldn't safely use it. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, restore the app window if it's minimized and move it so it fits fully on a screen. SMTO can only click a control that is actually showing on a connected screen.
  2. Scroll the app or open the section, tab or menu that contains the button or field so you can see it. Controls scrolled out of view or tucked inside a closed section count as hidden.
  3. Ask SMTO to look at the app again, then do the action. SMTO checks again where the control is before it clicks.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next step in the task completes the action on the control.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name and the control you wanted, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't ask SMTO to guess where the control is and click that spot; it could press the wrong thing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The target UI element is marked not visible or lacks positive on-screen geometry for an element-centred pointer action.

What this means

  • The target was marked not visible or lacked usable positive geometry for an element-centered pointer action. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The target was marked not visible or lacked usable positive geometry for an element-centered pointer action.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect visibility and bounds in the current window; do not force coordinates from stale or absent geometry.

How to fix it

  • Make the control visible through supported application actions (scroll, expand, restore the window, move it onto a connected display), then take a fresh ui.snapshot and check the element's visible state and bounds before interacting. A pointer click needs a centre point inside a display reported by Screen.
  • Make the intended control visible through supported application actions, then inspect its current reference and bounds.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway. Correct the target or prerequisites before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended control becomes visible with valid current bounds before interaction.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
